segments.text: Every day I post the same idea to my Buffer channels, and every day I rewrite it by hand for each network.
So I built Cascade on the Buffer API. One idea becomes a post for each of my Buffer channels.
I sign in with my Buffer account, and Cascade loads my channels from Buffer.
I add an image. I can upload one, or paste a link, and Cascade checks that Buffer can fetch it.
I pick which Buffer channels get it.
Cascade writes a version for each network.
Every post is checked against Buffer's own character limits, including my X Premium limit from Buffer.
It keeps my words, and never adds hashtags or emojis I didn't write.
I can edit any post, or ask for a fresh version.
For each channel I choose how Buffer handles it: my Buffer queue, a set time, or a Buffer draft.
One tap sends everything to Buffer. My idea is saved in Buffer Ideas, and each channel gets its own Buffer post.
It's all in my Buffer now, ready to go out.
Cascade, built on the Buffer API. One idea, every channel, ready in Buffer.
